summary.headline: HPL Electric Q2 FY27 revenue rose 40% YoY to ₹608 crore, a record, but EBITDA margin slipped to 11.74%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 40% YoY to ₹608 crore, the first quarter above ₹600 crore, taking H1 revenue to ₹1,124 crore (up 37%). Consumer and Industrial (C&I) revenue grew 64% to ₹337 crore and was about 55% of quarterly revenue, while Metering and Systems grew 18% to ₹271 crore. Q2 EBITDA rose 8% to ₹71 crore and PAT rose to ₹23 crore, but the EBITDA margin fell to 11.74% from 12.26% in Q1 on input cost inflation and mix. The Board also gave in-principle approval to evaluate a restructuring, possibly a scheme of arrangement to separate one or more businesses.

segments.name: Consumer and Industrial (C&I)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹337 crore, up 64% YoY and about 55% of quarterly revenue; H1 ₹615 crore, up 60%. Management said full-year C&I revenue should comfortably exceed the ₹1,000 crore it had indicated.

segments.name: Wires and cables (within C&I)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹178 crore, up 159% YoY; H1 ₹324 crore, about 95% of FY26 full-year revenue. Growth is now mostly volume-led, with telecom, real estate, retail, panel builders and OEMs cited as drivers.

segments.name: Lighting and switchgear (within C&I)
segments.commentary: Lighting grew 59% YoY, domestic switchgear 43% YoY, and industrial switchgear 29% QoQ. Management plans a revamped lighting range around ELECRAMA in February; fans are a new category with pan-India launch targeted for summer 2027.

segments.name: Metering and Systems
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹271 crore, up 18% YoY and 14% QoQ; H1 ₹509 crore, up 17%. Order book of ₹2,700 crore gives visibility beyond the current year, though quarterly conversion depends on customer schedules.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 FY27 to be much better than H1 in revenue across C&I and smart metering; FY28 sales plan is almost ready.
EBITDA margin expected to stabilise around 12% (CFO: full-year 12–12.5%), with improvement later if geopolitical conditions ease.
C&I cost increases to be largely passed on by the close of Q3 FY27, with a one-to-two-month lag and further price increases lined up after Diwali.
Metering margins described as decent at 15%+ at current volumes, though fixed contracts prevent pass-through of input cost increases.
Retail outlets targeted to reach 100,000 by March 2027, and C&I doubling targeted over three years.
Smart water meter numbers expected next year (FY28) after pilots and approvals; specialty cable commercial production expected around June 2027.
Management says the company is growing well above industry figures and is prioritising balance sheet ratios (inventory, debtors) and working capital.
risks_watch: Margin pressure: Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 11.74%; recovery depends on pass-through of C&I price increases after Diwali and on geopolitical input costs.
Metering contracts are fixed-price, so metal, plastic and electronics inflation cannot be passed on; a further drop in tender prices could weigh on margins.
Smart meter installation delays and AMISP payment timing; deployment pace depends on government push and a 2028 deadline for phase one.
Working capital: management flagged stock and debtor ratios as a priority, implying pressure on cash conversion.
Restructuring (possible demerger) is at an early evaluation stage with no timeline; details and value impact are unknown.
Wire and cable growth will taper in percentage terms because the Q3–Q4 FY26 base is high.
Export ramp-up is slowed by supply-chain and freight delays to Africa and the Middle East.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, volume growth and the C&I platform, but cautious on margins; management repeatedly said 12% EBITDA should stabilise and was evasive on restructuring specifics and timing.
key_quotes: Revenue from operations grew 40% year-on-year to 608 crores, our highest ever quarterly revenue and the first time we have crossed 600 crore level.
I don't see the margins going down further from here, but at least in the C&I part it should start coming up.
So I think that definitely helps us a lot.
Whatever happens, it will be good for the shareholders, and it would definitely unlock a good amount of value for them.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins normalise in the second half, and what is the full-year margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA margin should stabilise around 12% and, when asked, confirmed a full-year range of 12–12.5%; C&I cost increases to be largely passed on by close of Q3 with a 1–2 month lag, and metering contracts are fixed so inflation cannot be passed through.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Adani's takeover of IntelliSmart and the smart meter tender landscape on HPL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it positive: HPL is an approved vendor with Adani and EESL and a preferred vendor with each independent AMISP; quantities to flow through Adani, including EESL's extra quantities. Management expects 15–20% growth in smart meter volumes and says the 2028 deadline for phase one drives demand.

qa_highlights.question: Is aggressive L1 pricing in tenders sustainable, and what is the breakeven volume for metering?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said aggressive pricing has not been sustainable historically and fewer established players will remain; current volumes give decent margins of 15%+, and the recent margin pressure is seen as a one-off from geopolitical material and supply-chain inflation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation across wires and cables and metering, and is further investment needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Metering utilisation about 70% with flexible capacity; wires and cables about 80% after adding 7–8 machines in six months, with more ordered. A 3-year capacity and new-product evaluation is under way, which would entail capex not yet quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the order book dip and for the rest of FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ₹2,700 crore metering order book is not material at 2,500–3,000 crore levels, with over 2 years of revenue visibility. H2 FY27 expected to be much better than H1; C&I to comfortably exceed the ₹1,000 crore indication (already ₹615 crore in H1); FY28 sales plan almost ready.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scope and timing of the restructuring and the smart water meter opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: On restructuring, management said it is an enabling provision at evaluation stage with no timeline, typically a demerger of B2B and B2C businesses, and it would unlock shareholder value. Smart water meters: pilots are done and approvals are pending, with meaningful numbers expected next year (FY28).

capex_capacity: Metering capacity utilisation around 70%, after heavy capex over the last two and a half years; management says capacity is flexible and has upside if government pushes implementation toward the 2028 phase-one deadline.
Wires and cables flexible manufacturing capacity utilisation around 80%; 7 to 8 new machines added in the last six months, with more machines ordered on a staggered basis.
Management is evaluating capacity additions, including new wire and cable products, over the next 3 years; this would entail capex but is under evaluation with no amount disclosed.
Specialty cable commercial production expected around June 2027; full business plan and investment details to be shared once in place, likely in 2 to 3 years.
Lighting revamp with new smart lighting range targeted for ELECRAMA in February; fans to be addressed pan-India from summer 2027.
demand_pricing: Metering order book of ₹2,700 crore as on 2 Nov 2026; management said the absolute level (₹2,500–3,000 crore) is not material, with over 2 years of revenue visibility and monthly order inflows.
C&I order book reflects only about 15–20 days of orders; daily order flow described as healthy.

C&I cost increases partly passed on in Q2, with further price increases lined up after Diwali; pass-through expected largely by close of Q3 FY27 with a one-to-two-month lag. Lighting prices have stabilised and started rising after falling for about four years.

Wire and cable growth now mostly volume-led after earlier copper-price-driven value growth; demand cited from real estate, telecom, retail, panel builders and OEMs. Percentage growth to taper because Q3–Q4 FY26 base is high.

Metering fixed-price contracts prevent pass-through of metal, plastic and electronics inflation; current metering margins described as decent at 15%+. Management expects 15–20% smart meter volume growth.
Exports: first good African order received including advance; Africa and Middle East deliveries slowed by supply-chain and freight delays; FTAs expected to help.

tone.note: Management was confident on C&I growth, metering order visibility and smart meter demand, but cautious on margins (12-12.5% full year) and evasive on restructuring timing; analysts pressed on margin normalisation, aggressive L1 tender pricing and capacity needs.
